newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudan says rebels must forsake foreign help.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says rebels must forsake foreign help.

text.p: A Sudanese minister was quoted on Sunday as saying his government would hold talks with rebels fighting in the south and east if they called on the Ethiopian and Eritrean troops helping them to withdraw.

"The rebels must clearly denounce the Ethiopian invasion of Kurmuk and Qeissan," Cabinet Affairs Minister Salah-Eddin Karrar told the London-based Arabic daily Asharq al-Awsat, referring to towns on the Ethiopian border which fell to the rebels early last month.
"They must also request the Ethiopian government to stop its aggression against Sudan and withdraw its troops immediately. The same applies to troops on the Eritrean front.
"These are the necessary (preconditions) for any mediation effort," he added.

Sudan says that Eritrean and Ethiopian troops are helping rebels fight its Islamist government. Both countries deny any involvement in the conflict and the rebels say that they alone are waging the offensive.

Karrar said that Sudan welcomed mediation offers made by both the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia. Officials at the opposition National Democratic Alliance say that they will only hold talks with the Khartoum government about the way it would relinquish its power to them.

Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir overthrew the democratically-elected government of then prime minister Sadeq al-Mahdi in 1989. Mahdi held talks recently in the region to bolster support for the opposition he now heads.
